exercise.name: Lever Triceps Dip (plate loaded)

reference.title: Lever Triceps Dip (plate loaded)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Plate-loaded seated dip machine (iso-lateral lever arms)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the handles rise, breathe out as you press down.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 1.3 s press

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Plate load is user-chosen: start with light plates on the horns and press with the back on the pad.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Sit tall with the back on the pad and the feet flat; neutral grip on the handles beside the hips, arms straight down.
Breathe in and let the handles rise along the arc until the elbows bend to about 90 degrees, elbows pointing back.
Pause with the elbows bent and close to the sides; shoulders down, chest up.
Breathe out and press the handles down until the arms are straight beside the trunk.
Squeeze the triceps at the bottom with the shoulders down.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders shrugging up as the handles rise
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down away from the ears.
Keep the elbows pointing back, close to the trunk.
Sit tall with the back on the pad.
Stop with the elbows at about 90 degrees.

kinematics.peak: ≈119° at the top of the arc
kinematics.norm: From straight at the bottom to about 90 degrees at the top of the arc (clinical opinion)
The upper arms move from beside the trunk to behind it as the handles rise (clinical opinion)
Neutral: palms facing in on handles that run fore and aft (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pivot 94.1 cm high, -48.6 cm behind the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Lever swings 26.2°; hands within 0.39 cm of the arc
kinematics.norm: The handles ride the lever arc beside the trunk (clinical opinion)
Dips load the triceps heavily and the shoulder through extension (Boehler 2011; McKenzie 2022)

kinematics.setup: Pause 0.5 s with the arms straight
kinematics.peak: 2 s up, 0.3 s pause, 1.3 s press
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s up and 1-1.5 s press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #4247, Lever Triceps Dip (plate loaded), video (movement reference)
Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse)
McKenzie, Crowley-McHattan, Meir, Whitting and Volschenk 2022, bench, bar, and ring dips: do kinematics and muscle activity differ? (Int J Environ Res Public Health 19(20):13211; PMC9603242)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Plate load is user-chosen: start light; keep the shoulders down throughout.
Shoulder pain at the top of the arc: shorten the range.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: stop the handles lower (elbows less bent).

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the handles (Boehler 2011).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the handles (Boehler 2011).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Lower fibres pull the arm down and forward.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Lower fibres pull the arm down and forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Controls the shoulder as the arm goes behind the trunk.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Controls the shoulder as the arm goes behind the trunk.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall on the pad.
